title: CRIT-7: Mark issues triaged with rodgers:triaged label
acceptance_criteria: Every issue processed by triage gets rodgers:triaged=true label (or rodgers:triaged label added) so subsequent runs only process new/changed issues - idempotent triage

title: CRIT-6: Route docs to issue-templates workflow
acceptance_criteria: Issues classified as docs get rodgers:docs label, routed to issue-templates workflow for template improvements or documentation updates

title: CRIT-5: Route features to feature-bug workflow
acceptance_criteria: Issues classified as feature get rodgers:feature label, priority assessed (P1-P4) via keywords and LLM, routed to feature-bug workflow for spec development and implementation tracking

title: CRIT-4: Route bugs to feature-bug workflow with severity
acceptance_criteria: Issues classified as bug get rodgers:bug label, severity assessed (critical/high/medium/low) via keywords and LLM, routed to feature-bug workflow for reproduction and fix tracking

title: CRIT-3: Route questions to question-routing workflow
acceptance_criteria: Issues classified as question get rodgers:question label and are routed to question-routing workflow (doc link, code search, or doc-gap bead) within same triage run

title: CRIT-2: Classify issue type with LLM fallback
acceptance_criteria: Each issue classified as bug, feature, question, docs, chore, or unknown using label heuristics first (bug, enhancement, question, documentation), then LLM classification on title+body for unlabeled issues

title: CRIT-1: Triage runs on schedule and on issue events
acceptance_criteria: Triage workflow runs on configurable cron (default hourly) AND on GitHub issue events (opened, edited, labeled, unlabeled) - processes all open issues with rodgers:triaged=false

title: CRIT-7: Release bead filed with full metadata for audit
acceptance_criteria: Release bead filed with version, tag, branch, release URL, PR count by type, release notes hash, timestamp, and trigger source (scheduled/manual) - serves as audit trail

title: CRIT-6: Config-driven release schedule and branches
acceptance_criteria: Release schedule (cron), target branches (main, release-*), version bump rules, and backport label patterns defined in YAML config, not hardcoded

title: CRIT-5: Auto-backport labels trigger backport workflow
acceptance_criteria: PRs merged to main with labels backport:release-X.Y trigger automatic backport bead creation targeting release-X.Y branch with cherry-pick validation

title: CRIT-4: Publish GitHub Release with generated notes
acceptance_criteria: GitHub Release created at vX.Y.Z tag with full generated release notes, marked as latest release, draft=false, prerelease=false for stable versions

title: CRIT-3: Create release branch and tag with semantic version
acceptance_criteria: Rodgers creates release/vX.Y.Z branch from main, tags as vX.Y.Z with annotated tag message containing release notes summary

title: CRIT-2: Generate release notes from PR titles and labels
acceptance_criteria: Release notes generated with sections: Features (feat PRs), Bug Fixes (fix PRs), Documentation (docs PRs), Refactors (refactor PRs), Performance (perf PRs), Tests (test PRs), Chores (chore PRs) - each entry links to PR

title: CRIT-1: Detect release candidacy from merged PRs since last tag
acceptance_criteria: On schedule or manual trigger, Rodgers queries GitHub for merged PRs since last release tag, groups by type (feat, fix, chore, docs, refactor, perf, test), determines version bump (major/minor/patch) via conventional commits

title: CRIT-6: Config-driven question routing keywords
acceptance_criteria: Question routing keywords (how do i, how to, what is, why does, where can i find, explain, clarify, walk me through) are configurable in YAML, not hardcoded, with pattern matching and LLM fallback

title: CRIT-5: Label question issues with rodgers:question immediately
acceptance_criteria: When a GitHub issue is detected as a question (via question-routing keywords or LLM classification), Rodgers adds label rodgers:question within one triage run before any routing decision

title: CRIT-4: Zero tolerance for hallucination - route to human or file doc-gap
acceptance_criteria: Rodgers NEVER guesses or hallucinates answers - every question routes to existing docs, source code, or files doc-gap bead for human response

title: CRIT-3: File doc-gap bead only after exhausting docs and code search
acceptance_criteria: When a question issue exists, no docs answer it, and source code search yields no clear answer, Rodgers files a doc-gap bead with question title, user, link to issue, areas searched (docs files, code paths), and label rodgers:needs-doc

title: CRIT-2: Search source code for implementation questions before filing doc-gap bead
acceptance_criteria: When a question issue exists and no docs answer it, Rodgers searches source code if question is about implementation details (keywords: how does, what function, which module, internals, implementation, source code, walk me through, flow of, under the hood) before filing doc-gap bead

title: CRIT-1: Question issue with answer in docs gets doc link comment within one triage run
acceptance_criteria: When a question issue exists and docs exist that answer it, Rodgers posts a comment within one triage run with the correct doc link (docs/filename.md §section-title)

title: CRIT-7: Bug with all template fields populated transitions to ready-for-review without additional info requests
acceptance_criteria: A bug report with all required template fields populated (Environment, Steps to Reproduce, Expected Behavior, Actual Behavior) transitions to ready-for-review without requesting additional information

title: CRIT-6: Default template fields map to completeness requirements in feature-bug/question-routing plans
acceptance_criteria: All default template fields map to a completeness requirement in plans/feature-bug-plan.md or plans/question-routing-plan.md (Environment, Steps to Reproduce, Expected/Actual Behavior for bugs; Use Case, Proposed Behavior, Acceptance Criteria for features; Question, Context for questions)

title: CRIT-5: On reformat approval, post reformatted content for review before applying
acceptance_criteria: When requestor approves a reformat, Rodgers posts the reformatted content as a comment for requestor review before applying it to the issue body

title: CRIT-4: Never reformat issue without requestor's explicit approval
acceptance_criteria: Rodgers never reformats an issue without the requestor's explicit approval (reformat_consent: true, always ask before reformatting)

title: CRIT-3: Non-conforming issue gets reformat offer comment within one triage run
acceptance_criteria: A non-conforming issue (filed without template marker) receives a reformat offer comment within one triage run

title: CRIT-2: File bead with suggested default templates when none found and auto_suggest=true
acceptance_criteria: When project has no templates and auto_suggest: true, Rodgers files a bead with suggested default templates within one triage run

title: CRIT-1: Detect bug_report.md, feature_request.md, question.md in .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ on startup
acceptance_criteria: On startup, Rodgers detects whether .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ contains bug_report.md, feature_request.md, and question.md

title: AC-7: rogers init is idempotent (safe to re-run, same input = same result)
acceptance_criteria: rogers init is safe to re-run (idempotent): running multiple times with --fix produces same result as running once; all API calls use create-if-missing semantics for labels and discussion categories

title: AC-6: rogers init produces structured report with severity, description, fixability
acceptance_criteria: rogers init produces structured report with severity (BLOCKER/WARN/INFO), description, and fixability (auto/manual/na) for each check: issue templates, required labels, repo settings, release workflow, general workflows, discussion categories, branch protection, agent instructions, rogers.yaml

title: AC-5: rogers init reports blockers for missing issue templates and release workflow
acceptance_criteria: rogers init reports blockers for missing issue templates (.github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ with bug_report.md, feature_request.md, question.md) and missing release-capable GitHub Actions workflow with specific instructions for manual fix

title: AC-4: rogers init --fix creates missing discussion categories via GitHub API
acceptance_criteria: rogers init --repo owner/repo --fix creates missing discussion categories via GitHub API (Release Proposals category for release approval workflow)

title: AC-3: rogers init --fix creates missing required labels via GitHub API
acceptance_criteria: rogers init --repo owner/repo --fix creates missing required labels via GitHub API (bug, feature, question, needs-information, needs-documentation, ready-for-review, will-not-do, ready-for-work, in-progress) with canonical colors

title: AC-2: rogers init exits 1 on any blocker failure, lists all blockers
acceptance_criteria: rogers init --repo owner/repo exits with code 1 when any blocker check fails, listing all blockers (missing issue templates, missing required labels, no release workflow, main branch unprotected)

title: AC-1: rogers init exits 0 when all blocker checks pass
acceptance_criteria: rogers init --repo owner/repo exits with code 0 when all blocker checks pass (issue templates, required labels, release workflow, branch protection on main)

title: CRIT-7: Never moves to ready-for-review without minimum required information
acceptance_criteria: Rodgers never moves an issue to ready-for-review without the minimum required information for the issue type (bug: behavior observed/expected, reproduction steps, environment; feature: use case, proposed behavior, acceptance criteria)

title: CRIT-6: All GitHub issue acceptance criteria copied into epic bead description
acceptance_criteria: All acceptance criteria from the GitHub issue are copied into the epic bead description

title: CRIT-5: Each child bead is self-contained, implementable without consulting others
acceptance_criteria: Each child bead is self-contained: a developer reading only that bead can implement it without consulting other beads or parent epic (single codebase part, no 'and then...' descriptions)

title: CRIT-4: Human ready-for-work triggers epic + child beads within one triage run
acceptance_criteria: When human applies ready-for-work label and removes ready-for-review, Rodgers creates epic bead followed by child beads within one triage run

title: CRIT-3: Human will-not-do triggers closure comment and issue close within one triage run
acceptance_criteria: When human applies will-not-do label and removes ready-for-review, Rodgers posts closure comment acknowledging decision and closes issue within one triage run

title: CRIT-2: Incomplete bug/feature gets needs-information with specific missing fields
acceptance_criteria: A bug or feature issue with any required information field missing applies needs-information label and requests only the missing specific fields (not generic request)

title: CRIT-1: Complete bug/feature issue transitions to ready-for-review within one triage run
acceptance_criteria: A bug or feature issue with all required information fields populated (bug: behavior observed/expected, reproduction steps, environment; feature: use case, proposed behavior, acceptance criteria) transitions to ready-for-review within one triage run

title: AC-7: rogers doctor --fix prompts for confirmation before each fix
acceptance_criteria: rogers doctor --fix prompts for confirmation before applying each fix (Option A: close orphaned GitHub issue, Option B: reopen bead and link to correct issue, Option C: file new bead and close orphaned bead) and is not auto-destructive

title: AC-6: rogers doctor identifies in-progress beads linked to closed GitHub issues
acceptance_criteria: rogers doctor correctly identifies drift: beads marked in-progress but linked GitHub issue has been closed

title: AC-5: rogers doctor identifies closed beads linked to open GitHub issues
acceptance_criteria: rogers doctor correctly identifies drift: beads with status=closed but linked GitHub issue is open

title: AC-4: rogers doctor fails fast on config and auth before beads/repo
acceptance_criteria: rogers doctor fails fast on config and auth problems before checking beads or repo categories

title: AC-3: rogers doctor --verbose lists every drift event with details
acceptance_criteria: rogers doctor --verbose lists every individual drift event with GitHub issue URL, bead ID, and specific mismatch (closed bead/open issue, in-progress bead/closed issue, orphan beads, ready-for-work issues with no bead, release-proposed issues not in milestone, AGENTS.md convention violations)

title: AC-2: rogers doctor exits 1 on any category failure or drift detected
acceptance_criteria: rogers doctor exits with code 1 when any category (config, auth, beads, plans, repo) fails or drift is detected, listing all failures

title: AC-1: rogers doctor exits 0 when all categories pass with no drift
acceptance_criteria: rogers doctor exits with code 0 when config, auth, beads, plans, repo categories all pass and no drift detected

title: CRIT-12: Security patch detection via GH Advisory, security label, or CVE pattern
acceptance_criteria: Rodgers detects security patch via: GH Advisory match (repository.advisories()), security label on issue (or rogation.security_label), or CVE pattern (CVE-\d{4}-\d{4,}) in commit message or issue body; security patches filed as priority=1 beads

title: CRIT-11: Vote tiebreaking - most recent vote wins, 👎 always halts
acceptance_criteria: Vote tiebreaking: most recent vote wins always. 👎 before PR creation halts; once PR created vote locked; conflicting simultaneous votes resolve to 👎; votes on stale-closed Discussion ignored

title: CRIT-10: Close stale Discussion after stale_threshold_days, file revisit bead
acceptance_criteria: If no human response within release.stale_threshold_days (total), Rodgers closes Discussion, files revisit bead, does not proceed with backport

title: CRIT-9: Reminder comment if no response within voting_window_days
acceptance_criteria: If no 👍 or 👎 reaction received within release.voting_window_days, Rodgers posts a reminder comment on the Discussion

title: CRIT-8: 👎 reaction halts backport and posts acknowledgment within one triage run
acceptance_criteria: A 👎 reaction (or rejection comment) on approval Discussion halts backport and Rodgers posts comment acknowledging rejection and asking for guidance within one triage run

title: CRIT-7: Backport approval Discussion contains commit SHA, message, issue number, target branch
acceptance_criteria: Backport approval Discussion body contains at minimum: commit SHA, commit message, source GitHub issue number, target release branch — all extracted from merged commit and linked issue at creation time

title: CRIT-6: Close backport bead and check release completeness on PR merge
acceptance_criteria: When backport PR merges, Rodgers closes corresponding backport bead and checks if all critical backports merged for version, files bead suggesting patch release if complete

title: CRIT-5: File conflict-resolution bead on merge conflicts, no autonomous resolution
acceptance_criteria: If backport has merge conflicts, Rodgers files a conflict-resolution bead (rodgers:type=backport-conflict) and posts alert comment, but does not attempt autonomous conflict resolution

title: CRIT-4: Human approval triggers backport branch and PR creation within one triage run
acceptance_criteria: A human 👍 approval triggers creation of backport branch (backport/{sha_short}/{branch_name}) and PR targeting correct release branch within one triage run

title: CRIT-3: Create GitHub Discussion for each backport and wait for human approval
acceptance_criteria: Rodgers creates a GitHub Discussion for each backport in the release.approval_discussion_category and waits for human approval before opening a PR

title: CRIT-2: File backport bead for each target branch within one triage run
acceptance_criteria: Rodgers files a backport bead for each target release branch within one triage run of detecting the backport candidate

title: CRIT-1: Identify active release branches within one triage run of bug/security/backport-me merge
acceptance_criteria: When bug fix, security patch, or backport-me labeled issue merges to main, Rodgers identifies all active release branches (released, not EOL, not closed) within one triage run

title: AC-10: Release manager proposes releases via GitHub Discussion with approval gate
acceptance_criteria: Release manager monitors release readiness criteria, creates Release Proposal Discussion in configured category, waits for human 👍 approval, creates release branch/tag/GitHub Release atomically, handles 👎 halt and stale proposal follow-up

title: AC-9: Backport manager detects candidates and files beads with approval flow
acceptance_criteria: Backport manager evaluates merged commits for bug/security/doc fixes, identifies active release branches, creates backport beads per target branch, files GitHub Discussion for approval, waits for human 👍 before creating PR branch

title: AC-8: Question router searches docs and code before filing doc gaps
acceptance_criteria: Question router searches docs/**/*.md and all source code files for implementation questions (keywords: how does, what function, which module, internals, implementation, source code, walk me through, flow of, under the hood), answers from code don't create doc-gap beads

title: AC-7: Epic/child bead breakdown for epic-scale work
acceptance_criteria: Epic bead creation with child beads: all children start deferred, human signal required to batch-open, orphan detection on each triage run, LLM analyzes work areas and creates self-contained child beads

title: AC-6: State machine implements all triage workflow states
acceptance_criteria: State machine implements: NEW_UNCLASSIFIED, BUG/FEATURE/QUESTION_INCOMPLETE, NEEDS_INFO, STALE, SEARCH_DOCS, DOC_FOUND, DOC_GAP, READY_FOR_REVIEW, WILL_NOT_DO, READY_FOR_WORK, FILE_EPIC_BEADS, IN_PROGRESS with correct transitions

title: AC-5: Triage engine with LLM classification and structured output validation
acceptance_criteria: Triage engine classifies issues (bug/feature/question) via LLM with structured output validator, respects existing human labels, defaults to question on uncertainty, applies bot_labels for bot authors

title: AC-4: GitHub API client with token auth and rate limit handling
acceptance_criteria: GitHub API client implements token authentication, required scopes (repo, read:org), rate limit detection with warning at <100 remaining, and exponential backoff retry logic

title: AC-3: Beads database schema with required tables and columns
acceptance_criteria: Beads database (Dolt) has tables: epics, children, state with columns for github_issue_url, github_issue_state, rodgers_type, rodgers_parent, rodgers_labels, discovered_from, acceptance_criteria, priority, status, title, description

title: AC-2: Config validation fails fast with descriptive errors
acceptance_criteria: rogers doctor --category config validates config.yaml and fails fast with descriptive errors for missing file, malformed YAML, missing required keys, invalid scheduler.interval_minutes, placeholder github.token, empty release.active_branches, and rogation.labels_never_bot_managed containing Rodgers-required labels

title: AC-1: Configuration schema defines all required keys
acceptance_criteria: Configuration schema in code defines all required keys: github.owner, github.repo, github.token, scheduler.interval_minutes, beads.remote, beads.database, release.active_branches, rogation.labels_never_bot_managed

title: Triage Workflow Plan Implementation
description:
Plan: plans/triage-workflow-plan.md

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] CRIT-1: A new issue with a recognized template appears in the triage queue within one polling interval of creation
- [ ] CRIT-2: An issue missing a recognized template receives a single reformat offer comment within one polling interval; no repeat offers
- [ ] CRIT-3: A question issue receives an answer OR a doc-gap bead within one polling interval
- [ ] CRIT-4: A feature or bug issue transitions to ready-for-review only when all completeness requirements in plans/feature-bug-plan.md are satisfied
- [ ] CRIT-5: When an external user comments on a question issue, Rodgers re-evaluates the issue within one polling interval
- [ ] CRIT-6: Every triage evaluation is recorded in a bead (rodgers:type=triage) with issue number, decision, reason, and timestamp
- [ ] CRIT-7: Triage beads are append-only; they are never edited after creation
acceptance_criteria: Triage workflow fully implemented per plan

title: Release Management Plan Implementation
description:
Plan: plans/release-management-plan.md

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] CRIT-1: After each successful merge to main, Rodgers computes next version (patch by default, minor for feat:, major for BREAKING CHANGE) using Conventional Commits
- [ ] CRIT-2: Rodgers creates an annotated Git tag matching computed version and pushes it to origin
- [ ] CRIT-3: Rodgers generates CHANGELOG.md entries grouped by type (feat, fix, chore, docs, refactor, perf, test) from conventional commits since last tag
- [ ] CRIT-4: Rodgers creates a GitHub Release with the tag, title 'Release vX.Y.Z', and generated changelog as release notes
- [ ] CRIT-5: On any failure (tag push, changelog write, release create), Rodgers files a bead with failure details and retries on next successful merge
- [ ] CRIT-6: All release operations happen in the bead context with audit trail
- [ ] CRIT-7: Release beads link to the merge commit that triggered them
acceptance_criteria: Release management fully implemented per plan

title: Question Routing Plan Implementation
description:
Plan: plans/question-routing-plan.md

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] CRIT-1: When a question issue exists and docs exist that answer it, Rodgers posts a comment within one triage run with the correct doc link
- [ ] CRIT-2: When a question issue exists and no docs answer it, Rodgers searches the source code if the question is about implementation details before filing a doc-gap bead
- [ ] CRIT-3: When Rodgers finds an answer in the source code, it posts a plain-language explanation citing the relevant file, function, and line numbers, then closes the issue if fully answered
- [ ] CRIT-4: When a chore bead (rodgers:type=docs) is closed, Rodgers verifies the GitHub issue has a documentation link comment; if the link is missing, Rodgers posts it within one triage run; if the issue is already closed, Rodgers posts the link comment anyway; on GitHub API read failure, Rodgers retries on the next triage run without alerting
- [ ] CRIT-5: Rodgers never closes a question issue without either answering it or filing a chore bead (rodgers:type=docs)
- [ ] CRIT-6: Rodgers never routes a non-question issue through this workflow
acceptance_criteria: Question routing fully implemented per plan

title: Issue Templates Plan Implementation
description:
Plan: plans/issue-templates-plan.md

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] CRIT-1: On startup, Rodgers detects whether .github/ISSUE_TEMPLATE/ contains bug_report.md, feature_request.md, and question.md
- [ ] CRIT-2: When a project has no templates and auto_suggest: true, Rodgers files a bead with suggested default templates within one triage run
- [ ] CRIT-3: A non-conforming issue (filed without template marker) receives a reformat offer comment within one triage run
- [ ] CRIT-4: Rodgers never reformats an issue without the requestor's explicit approval
- [ ] CRIT-5: When a requestor approves a reformat, Rodgers posts the reformatted content as a comment for requestor review before applying it
- [ ] CRIT-6: All default template fields map to a completeness requirement in plans/feature-bug-plan.md or plans/question-routing-plan.md
- [ ] CRIT-7: A bug report with all required template fields populated transitions to ready-for-review without requesting additional information
acceptance_criteria: Issue templates fully implemented per plan

title: Init Plan Implementation
description:
Plan: plans/init-plan.md

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] AC-1: rogers init --repo owner/repo exits 0 when all blocker checks pass
- [ ] AC-2: rogers init --repo owner/repo exits 1 when any blocker check fails, listing all blockers
- [ ] AC-3: rogers init --repo owner/repo --fix creates missing required labels via GitHub API
- [ ] AC-4: rogers init --repo owner/repo --fix creates missing discussion categories via GitHub API
- [ ] AC-5: rogers init reports blocks for missing issue templates and missing release workflow with specific instructions
- [ ] AC-6: rogers init produces a structured report with severity, description, and fixability for each check
- [ ] AC-7: rogers init is safe to re-run (idempotent: same input = same result)
acceptance_criteria: Init command fully implemented per plan

title: Feature & Bug Request Handling Plan Implementation
description:
Plan: plans/feature-bug-plan.md

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] CRIT-1: A bug or feature issue with all required information fields populated transitions to ready-for-review within one triage run
- [ ] CRIT-2: A bug or feature issue with any required information field missing applies needs-information and requests only the missing specific fields (not a generic request)
- [ ] CRIT-3: When a human applies will-not-do, Rodgers posts a closure comment and closes the issue within one triage run
- [ ] CRIT-4: When a human applies ready-for-work, Rodgers creates an epic bead followed by child beads within one triage run
- [ ] CRIT-5: Each child bead is self-contained: a developer reading only that bead can implement it without consulting other beads or the parent epic
- [ ] CRIT-6: All acceptance criteria from the GitHub issue are copied into the epic bead description
- [ ] CRIT-7: Rodgers never moves an issue to ready-for-review without the minimum required information for the issue type
acceptance_criteria: Feature & bug request handling fully implemented per plan

title: Doctor Plan Implementation
description:
Plan: plans/doctor-plan.md

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] AC-1: rogers doctor exits 0 when all categories pass with no drift
- [ ] AC-2: rogers doctor exits 1 when any category fails or drift is detected, listing all failures
- [ ] AC-3: rogers doctor --verbose lists every individual drift event with GitHub issue URL, bead ID, and the specific mismatch
- [ ] AC-4: rogers doctor fails fast on config and auth problems before checking beads or repo
- [ ] AC-5: rogers doctor correctly identifies closed beads linked to open GitHub issues
- [ ] AC-6: rogers doctor correctly identifies in-progress beads linked to closed GitHub issues
- [ ] AC-7: rogers doctor --fix prompts for confirmation before applying each fix and is not auto-destructive
acceptance_criteria: Doctor command fully implemented per plan

title: Backport Plan Implementation
description:
Plan: plans/backport-plan.md

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] CRIT-1: When a bug fix, security patch, or backport-me labeled issue is merged to main, Rodgers identifies all active release branches within one triage run
- [ ] CRIT-2: Rodgers files a backport bead for each target branch within one triage run of detecting the candidate
- [ ] CRIT-3: Rodgers creates a GitHub Discussion for each backport and waits for human approval before opening a PR
- [ ] CRIT-4: A human approval triggers the creation of a backport branch and PR targeting the correct release branch within one triage run
- [ ] CRIT-5: If a backport has merge conflicts, Rodgers files a conflict-resolution bead and posts an alert comment, but does not attempt autonomous conflict resolution
- [ ] CRIT-6: When a backport PR is merged, Rodgers closes the corresponding backport bead and checks for release completeness
- [ ] CRIT-7: The backport approval Discussion body contains at minimum: the commit SHA, the commit message, the source GitHub issue number, and the target release branch — all extracted directly from the merged commit and linked issue at creation time
- [ ] CRIT-8: A rejection reaction on the approval Discussion halts the backport and Rodgers posts a comment acknowledging the rejection and asking for guidance within one triage run of detecting the reaction
- [ ] CRIT-9: If no approval reaction is received within release.voting_window_days, Rodgers posts a reminder comment on the Discussion
- [ ] CRIT-10: If no human response is received within release.stale_threshold_days (total, including the voting window and any pings), Rodgers closes the Discussion, files a revisit bead, and does not proceed with the backport
- [ ] CRIT-11: For backport approvals: any rejection before the backport PR is created halts the backport; once the PR is created the vote is locked and subsequent rejection is acknowledged but does not stop the work; conflicting simultaneous votes resolve to rejection (halt + ask for clarification); votes on a stale-closed Discussion are ignored
- [ ] CRIT-12: Rodgers detects a security patch when any of: GH Advisory match (via repository.advisories()), security label on the issue (or rogation.security_label), or CVE pattern (CVE-dddddddd) in commit message or issue body; detected security patches are filed as priority=1 beads
acceptance_criteria: Backport manager fully implemented per plan

title: Architecture Plan Implementation
description:
Plan: plans/architecture-plan.md

Acceptance Criteria:
- [ ] AC-1: Configuration schema validates all required keys (github.owner, github.repo, github.token, scheduler.interval_minutes, beads.remote, beads.database, llm.base_url, llm.model, llm.api_key)
- [ ] AC-2: GitHub API client authenticates with token and performs CRUD operations on issues, labels, discussions, PRs
- [ ] AC-3: Bead controller (bd CLI) creates, updates, queries beads with GitHub issue linkage (github_issue_url, github_issue_state, rodgers_type)
- [ ] AC-4: Triage engine runs on scheduler, classifies issues (bug/feature/question), applies labels
- [ ] AC-5: Feature/bug workflow routes to feature-bug-plan.md, questions route to question-routing-plan.md
- [ ] AC-6: Release manager evaluates release criteria, creates GitHub Discussion for approval
- [ ] AC-7: Backport manager evaluates closed issues on active branches, files beads for human review
- [ ] AC-8: Doctor command validates config, GitHub, beads, LLM, scheduler connectivity
- [ ] AC-9: Init command audits repo readiness, creates labels, templates, workflows
- [ ] AC-10: All GitHub operations go through GitHub API client (no raw HTTP)
- [ ] AC-11: All bead operations go through bead controller (bd CLI)
- [ ] AC-12: Scheduler runs triage loop on configured interval
- [ ] AC-13: Structured output validator wraps all LLM calls, validates JSON schema
- [ ] AC-14: Plan loader reads plans/*.md, extracts acceptance criteria for bead creation
- [ ] AC-15: Configuration supports rogers.yaml repo-level overrides merged with host config
- [ ] AC-16: Error handling with structured logging, retry logic for transient failures
- [ ] AC-17: Warm, respectful output in all user-facing text (CLI, GitHub comments, beads)
acceptance_criteria: All architecture components implemented and integrated per plan
